title: IgA nephropathy
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of iga-nephropathy-appraised-candidate-bf0656421814; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional editorial appraisal of iga-nephropathy-candidate-2a8f21ad71cc. Agent-authored preliminary appraisal of the frozen selected reports, not a systematic review. Abstract-only access limits critical quality assessment; independent study groups and dataset families have not been established. Weight concerns this bounded mechanism context, not clinical effectiveness or disease-wide importance. Context-mismatched treatment claims are excluded from mechanistic ratings. No calibration or independent reviewer decision is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: IL-6
entities.description: A cytokine; its effects here are assessed in IgA1-secreting cultures.

entities.label: IgA1-secreting cell lines
entities.description: Immortalized IgA1-producing cells used in the cited experiments; not a claim about every plasma cell.

entities.label: Galactose-deficient IgA1
entities.description: IgA1 with deficient galactose in hinge-region O-glycans.

entities.label: Antiglycan IgG
entities.description: IgG recognizing the glycan epitopes examined in these studies.

entities.label: IgA1-containing immune complexes
entities.description: Complexes containing IgA1; composition and molecular mass affect their measured activity.

entities.label: Mesangial cells
entities.description: Glomerular cells studied in culture and biopsy tissue.

entities.label: MAPK / ERK activation
entities.description: A contextual signalling process, with culture perturbations and biopsy associations.

entities.label: Renal inflammation / injury
entities.description: Renal injury outcomes; evidence and causal interpretation are specific to each linked study.

claims.text: Patient-derived immortalized IgA1-secreting cells produced IgA1 with galactose-deficient O-glycans.
limitations: Immortalized cultures; does not identify the dominant in-vivo source or establish sufficiency for disease.

claims.text: IL-6 accentuated IgA1 galactose deficiency in IgA1-secreting cultures, with a stronger response in patient-derived cells.
limitations: Culture glycosylation response; does not establish clinical benefit from IL-6 inhibition.

claims.text: Galactose-deficient IgA1 formed immune complexes with patient-derived glycan-specific IgG in vitro.
limitations: Formation requires the matching antibody; this edge alone does not establish renal injury.

claims.text: Patient-derived glycan-specific IgG bound galactose-deficient IgA1 and formed complexes in vitro.
limitations: Antibody specificity and assay context matter; serum associations are not proof of clinical causation.

claims.text: Large IgA1-containing serum-complex fractions stimulated proliferation of cultured mesangial cells.
limitations: In-vitro proliferation; activity depends on complex composition and molecular mass.

claims.text: Smaller complex fractions inhibited proliferation, qualifying a uniformly stimulatory interpretation.
limitations: Size-dependent culture effects do not establish the net in-vivo effect of every complex.

claims.text: Patient-derived large IgA1 complexes activated ERK signalling in cultured human mesangial cells.
limitations: The route involves CD71 and additional signalling; the diagram omits intermediate steps.

claims.text: IgA1-stimulated human mesangial cultures secreted IL-6; pathway blockade reduced secretion.
limitations: Culture perturbations; linking this branch to IgA1-producing cells is a cross-study hypothesis.

claims.text: Biopsy mesangial ERK activation was associated with higher proteinuria and elevated blood pressure.
limitations: Biopsy association does not prove that ERK activation caused renal injury.

claims.text: Uncomplexed IgA1 did not significantly alter proliferation in the reported mesangial-cell culture assay, limiting attribution of the complex effect to IgA1 alone.
limitations: This culture comparison does not establish the effects of uncomplexed IgA1 in vivo or in every mesangial context.

paragraphs.text: This bounded IgA nephropathy model follows galactose-deficient IgA1, glycan-specific IgG, immune-complex formation and mesangial responses. Patient-derived IgA1-secreting cultures produced galactose-deficient IgA1, and IL-6 accentuated that glycosylation abnormality in culture. Galactose-deficient IgA1 formed complexes with patient-derived glycan-specific IgG in vitro. Large IgA1-containing complex fractions stimulated cultured mesangial-cell proliferation and ERK signalling; stimulated mesangial cultures also secreted IL-6. These findings motivate a proposed connection between abnormal IgA1, complex-dependent mesangial activation and local inflammatory signalling.

Most functional links in this map come from cell-culture experiments rather than intervention in patients. Smaller complex fractions inhibited proliferation, and uncomplexed IgA1 did not significantly alter proliferation, so the complex effect cannot be attributed uniformly to IgA1 alone. Mesangial ERK activation in biopsies was associated with proteinuria and blood pressure, which does not establish its causal contribution to renal injury. The assembled pathway and any feedback interpretation remain provisional; this selected-report map is not a complete account of IgA nephropathy and does not synthesize treatment efficacy. An independent current-literature check should identify major missing mechanisms and any necessary expansion of its scope.
